name: Gadds' – The Ramsgate Brewery (beer shop & tasting room)
summary: Thanet's best-known independent brewery: buy or sample Gadds' ales at the brewery shop, with seasonal tours and open days.
description: Gadds' is the trading name of The Ramsgate Brewery, Thanet's longest-established modern brewer, whose cask ales such as No.5 and No.3 turn up in pubs all over East Kent. The brewery sits on Hornet Close on the Pyson's Road industrial estate between Ramsgate and Broadstairs, and it runs a beer shop and tasting room where you can buy bottles and casks to take away or try whatever is currently on. It is a working industrial unit rather than a pretty pub, so think of it as a place to stock up and chat to the brewers. Seasonal brewery tours are released as tickets through the online shop, and private tours can be arranged for groups of fifteen or more. Look out for tap-room events: in 2026 it held a Green Hop beer festival in October and has a 'Little Cracker' open day listed for early December.
address: Hornet Close, Pyson's Road Industrial Estate, Broadstairs
opening_hours: Shop/tasting room (as published Oct 2026): Thu 12:00-16:00, Fri 12:00-17:00, Sat 12:00-15:00.
price: Tour tickets released seasonally via the online shop; price not published at time of research.
tips: Little Cracker open day listed for Sat 5 Dec 2026, 12:00-17:00. Group tours (15+) by email to info@ramsgatebrewery.co.uk.

name: Shivering Sands Brewery & Tap Room
summary: Small Manston microbrewery and tap room named after the WWII sea forts; opens Friday and Saturday only.
description: Shivering Sands is a microbrewery on the Maple Leaf Business Park at Manston, only a few kilometres south of Birchington. Margate resident Gary Gould set it up at the end of 2019 and it began brewing in the summer of 2020. The name and logo come from the Shivering Sands Maunsell forts, the Second World War anti-aircraft towers in the Thames Estuary that later housed a 1960s pirate radio station. The tap room shares the two-storey brewery building and usually has at least a couple of its own beers to drink in or take away. It is a no-frills industrial-unit bar with limited opening, so check before making a special trip; CAMRA has noted winter closures in past years.
opening_hours: Per Thanet CAMRA (2026): Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat 12:00-17:00, closed Sun-Thu. Has closed for winter in past years.
tips: The brewery's old website no longer works; check Thanet CAMRA or its social media before you go.

name: The Lifeboat Ale & Cider House (Floc), Margate
summary: Old Town ale and cider house, now Floc brewery's Margate bar: cask and craft beer plus Kentish ciders.
description: The Lifeboat on Market Street in Margate's Old Town has long been one of Thanet's favourite real-ale and cider houses, a characterful bar of barrels and wooden furniture with cider served from the cask. It is now run as the Margate outpost of Floc, the Canterbury craft brewery, so alongside guest ales and Kentish ciders you can try Floc's own beers without travelling to their taproom. It is a few minutes' walk from Turner Contemporary and the harbour arm, which makes it an easy stop on a Margate day out from Birchington, just one stop away by train. The bar is walk-in only.
tips: No bookings – just walk in. Margate station is about 10 minutes' walk.

name: Floc Brewery & Taproom, Canterbury
summary: Craft brewery taproom on Cotton Road, Canterbury, with pizza, a quiz night and Floc beers fresh from the tanks.
description: Floc is a Canterbury craft brewery known for modern hop-forward and hazy beers. Its taproom sits next to the brewhouse on Cotton Road, on the south-west side of the city centre, and pours the beers fresh alongside pizza. It is a relaxed, casual space popular with locals and a good way to finish a Canterbury sightseeing day. A quiz runs on the first and third Thursday of each month (booking needed), and groups of six or more can reserve tables in advance. Floc also runs a container bar at Folkestone's Goods Yard and the Lifeboat in Margate.
opening_hours: Per Floc (Oct 2026): Thu 17:00-22:00, Fri-Sat 13:00-22:00, Sun 13:00-20:00. Pizza until 20:30 Thu-Sat, 17:30 Sun.
tips: Book ahead for groups of 6+ and for quiz nights.

name: The Foundry Brew Pub – Canterbury Brewers & Distillers
summary: Brewery and distillery in a Victorian foundry in central Canterbury; tours with tastings of beers, gins and rums.
description: Canterbury Brewers & Distillers make beer, gin, vodka, rum, moonshine and English whisky inside a converted Victorian foundry on Stour Street, in the heart of Canterbury. The brew pub and restaurant look straight through glass into the brewing and distilling equipment. Its spirits are made 'grain to glass' from English barley, and the company also produces spirits under the Anno name. Tours begin with a drink of your choice, take you behind the glass to see the brewery and stills, and finish with a guided tasting. In past summers the Foundry has also run special gin tours with Canterbury Cathedral, using herbs from the Cathedral's own herb garden.
opening_hours: Per its website (Oct 2026): Mon-Thu 12:00-22:00, Fri-Sat 12:00-23:30, Sun 12:00-19:00.
price: Tour & tasting £25 per person (Produced in Kent listing; includes welcome drink and guided tasting).
tips: Book tours online in advance. Easy walk from Canterbury East or West station.

name: Shepherd Neame Brewery Tours & Visitor Centre, Faversham
summary: Guided 80-minute tours of 'Britain's oldest brewer' in historic Faversham, ending with a tutored tasting.
description: Shepherd Neame calls itself Britain's oldest brewer and has brewed on Court Street in Faversham for centuries; its beers such as Spitfire and Bishops Finger are sold in pubs right across Kent, including several in Thanet. The visitor centre runs guided tours of about 80 minutes through the working brewery, including the Old Brewery Store, finishing in the visitor-centre bar with a tutored tasting of Kentish ales and lagers. There are also evening tours with an ale-sampler's supper and seasonal six-course beer-and-food matching dinners. Faversham is one of Kent's best-preserved market towns, so a tour pairs well with a wander along Abbey Street and the creek.
opening_hours: Scheduled morning and afternoon tours; Visit Swale lists Wednesday to Saturday. Check the online booking calendar.
price: Individual tour £25 per person (official site, Oct 2026); private groups from £275 per group of up to 10.
accessibility: Working industrial site; see the brewery's accessibility guide before booking.
tips: Over-18s only on brewery tours. Book ahead. National Rail Days Out 2-for-1 offer applies with a rail ticket – Faversham is on the line from Birchington. The Faversham Hop Festival is held in early September (5-6 Sep in 2026).

name: Simpsons' Wine Estate, Barham
summary: Award-winning English sparkling and still wine estate on the North Downs south of Canterbury; pre-booked tastings and tours.
description: Simpsons' Wine Estate was planted in 2012 by Charles and Ruth Simpson and has become one of East Kent's best-known producers of English sparkling and still wines. The vineyards lie on the chalk of the North Downs around Barham, in the Elham Valley south of Canterbury. Visits centre on the Glass House Tasting Room, which overlooks the winery. You can book a seated wine tasting on weekday afternoons, or a longer vineyard-and-winery tour that walks part of the Roman Road vineyard (weather permitting), explains still and Classic Method winemaking and ends with a tasting. Bottles can be bought at the cellar door afterwards.
address: The Barns, Church Lane, Barham, Canterbury
opening_hours: Office/cellar door 09:00-17:00 for wine purchases and collections; all tastings must be pre-booked.
price: Wine Tasting Experience £25; Vineyard & Winery Tour and Tasting £45 (autumn/winter, per Produced in Kent).
tips: Book online or by phone before travelling – no walk-in tastings. Designate a driver: roughly 35-40 minutes by car from Birchington.

name: Barnsole Vineyard, Staple
summary: Small boutique vineyard at Staple, the nearest wine estate to Thanet; Pinot Noir-led wines, tastings and tours.
description: Barnsole is a small vineyard at Staple, in the orchard and farm country between Wingham and Sandwich, about twenty minutes' drive from Birchington. It describes itself as a boutique Kent vineyard and makes much of Pinot Noir, linking the grape to the Roman legions who landed at nearby Richborough. Visitors are welcome to drop in to buy wine, and tastings and tours are offered. It is a quiet rural spot rather than a large visitor centre, so it suits a relaxed stop combined with Wingham, Sandwich or Richborough Roman Fort.
tips: Opening hours and tour prices were not shown on the pages we could read – phone ahead before visiting.

name: Woolton Farm & Kentish Pip Cider, Bekesbourne
summary: Family farm near Canterbury making Kentish Pip cider and Woolton wines; tasting flights in The Barn and summer tours.
description: Woolton Farm at Bekesbourne, just east of Canterbury, has been farmed by the Mount family for more than a hundred years. It is the home of Kentish Pip, an independent cider maker whose range includes the crisp Grafter, the hibiscus-and-raspberry Roselle and the reserve Skylark, and the farm also grows grapes for its Woolton wines, among them Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and a sparkling rosé. The Barn, which opened in 2020 as a simple coffee stop, has grown into a bar and restaurant where you can book cider and wine tasting flights, and the owners host cider and wine tours on selected summer dates. Camping and glamping pitches are close by.
price: Woolton wines £21-£36 a bottle (2026 site); tasting-flight prices on the booking page.
tips: Tours only run on set summer dates – check the events page; tasting flights can be pre-booked online.

name: Whitstable Oyster Farm Tour
summary: Two-hour guided walk onto Whitstable's oyster beds in borrowed waders, ending with freshly shucked oysters and a drink.
description: Whitstable has been famous for its oysters since Roman times, and the Whitstable Oyster Company runs guided tours of its farm on the foreshore beside the town. You meet on the beach just past the sea wall near Horsebridge, are kitted out with waders or wellies, and walk out over the soft ground to learn how oysters are grown, harvested and farmed responsibly. The tour ends with freshly shucked oysters and a glass of local sparkling wine, a Whitstable Brewery beer or a soft drink. Tours run all year and take about two hours, mostly outdoors, so dress for the weather.
address: Meeting point on the beach past the sea wall, near Horsebridge Road, Whitstable
opening_hours: Year-round on scheduled dates (book online).
accessibility: Uneven, soft foreshore; the operator says the tour is not suitable for visitors with accessibility requirements.
tips: Ages 12+ only (12-16 with an adult). Online bookings need a group of four or more; smaller groups email tours@whitstable.rocks. Arrive 15 minutes early. The town's Oyster Festival is held each summer, usually in July.

name: Time & Tide Taphouse, Sandwich (and brewery taproom)
summary: Sandwich bar of the local Time & Tide brewery; the farm taproom near Worth opens on summer weekends.
description: Time & Tide is a small craft brewery on Statenborough Farm, between Eastry and Worth just south of Sandwich, known for modern keg beers and for brewing with hops grown by the Deal Hop Farm community project. Its town bar, the Taphouse on Delf Street in medieval Sandwich, is the easiest place to try the range. The brewery's own farm taproom opened in 2022 and usually opens on Fridays and Saturdays in summer, serving its beers with Kentish cider and occasional street food. The brewery also organises a free 'Tinsel Town' craft-beer festival at St Mary's Arts Centre in Sandwich each December.
opening_hours: Taphouse: hours differ between listings – check the website or social media. Farm taproom (Statenborough Farm, Felderland Lane, CT14 0BX): per CAMRA Fri 15:00-18:00, Sat 12:00-18:00, mainly in summer.
tips: Tinsel Town Craft Beer Festival, St Mary's Arts Centre, Sandwich: Fri 18 Dec 2026 16:00-22:00 and Sat 19 Dec 12:00-22:00, free entry.

name: Docker Brewery & Taproom, Folkestone
summary: Folkestone craft brewery that began in a harbour shipping container; big new taproom pouring straight from the tanks.
description: Docker Brew Co started in 2016 in a shipping container in the East Yard of Folkestone Harbour, alongside its sister Docker Bakery. In January 2026 the brewery moved to a much larger unit on the Five Acre estate at Park Farm, on the edge of Folkestone, where the taproom serves fruity, hop-forward keg beers direct from 500-litre serving tanks, plus wine, cider and pizza. It hosts community events and live music, and the space can be hired for private parties. At roughly 45-50 minutes from Birchington it is at the edge of day-trip range, best combined with Folkestone's harbour arm and Creative Quarter.
address: Unit C, Five Acre Estate, Park Farm Road, Folkestone
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (updated June 2026): Fri 15:00-21:00, Sat 12:00-21:00, Sun 12:00-18:00; closed Mon-Thu.
tips: Keg beer only, no cask ale. Stagecoach bus 73 stops about 160 m away.

name: Chartham Vineyard
summary: Family vineyard in the Stour valley west of Canterbury; Saturday cellar door and owner-led tours with tutored tastings.
description: Chartham Vineyard is a family-run vineyard at Burnt House Farm in the Stour valley, just west of Canterbury, that pairs modern sustainable growing with traditional farming. Its shop opens on Saturdays in the old farm courtyard, and on Saturdays the owners lead pre-booked guided walks through the vines followed by a tutored tasting of their wines, which include a Bacchus and a Pinot Gris. Chartham has its own station on the Canterbury West to Ashford line, so you can visit without driving.
address: Burnt House Farm, Station Road, Chartham, Canterbury
opening_hours: Vineyard shop Saturdays 10:30-17:00 (2026 website). Tours Saturdays at 11:00 and 14:00, pre-booked.
price: Tour prices on the online shop.
tips: Pre-book tours online; ample free parking.

name: Goody Ales Brewery & 'The Cathedral' Taproom, Herne
summary: Rural brewery near Herne Bay with a wooden taproom and terrace over fields, known for 'Firkins at Full Moon' nights.
description: Goody Ales is a small brewery in the countryside on Braggs Lane at Herne, a short drive inland from Herne Bay. Its bar, nicknamed 'The Cathedral', is a wooden building with a terrace looking out over a field and woodland, serving the brewery's own beers along with Kent wines and ciders and, on some days, pizza and barbecue food. The brewery is known for its monthly 'Firkins at Full Moon' evenings on or near the full moon and for live music, and the building can be hired for weddings and parties. Goody's beers are also poured at the Beer on the Pier micropub in Herne Bay.
opening_hours: Last published by CAMRA (May 2024): Mon-Fri 16:00-19:00, Sat 10:00-18:00, Sun closed – not confirmed for 2026.
tips: The brewery website no longer resolves; check its social media before travelling.

name: Xylo, Margate (bar with cellar microbrewery)
summary: Margate Old Town bar with its own small brewery in the cellar, pouring house beers and guests; dog and family friendly.
description: Xylo is a bar on Margate's lower High Street, just behind the seafront, with a four-barrel brewery built into its cellar. Neil Wright and Ben Atkins set it up in 2019, and it is now one of the very few places in Thanet where the beer is brewed on the premises. Several house beers are usually on, mostly modern keg and canned styles rather than cask, alongside plenty of guest beers. It is relaxed and welcoming to families and dogs, with occasional DJ sessions, and sits a couple of minutes from the Lifeboat and Fez, so it is easy to combine them in a short Old Town crawl.
tips: Mostly keg beer – ask what was brewed downstairs.

name: Fez micropub, Margate
summary: Quirky Margate micropub stuffed with fairground and brewery memorabilia; cask ales and cider straight from the cellar.
description: Fez opened in December 2015 in a former card shop on Margate's High Street and quickly became one of the town's most talked-about micropubs; CAMRA's Good Beer Guide has called it a must-visit. The room is eclectically furnished with high and low tables and raised benches, and the walls are covered in brewery signs and old fairground bits and pieces, a nod to nearby Dreamland. Cask ales and ciders are served by gravity from a cooled cellar room behind the small bar, with the beers changing constantly and a short wine list. Like most micropubs it is about conversation rather than TVs or music.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (updated June 2026): Mon-Thu 15:00-23:00, Fri-Sat 12:00-23:30, Sun 12:00-22:00.
accessibility: Step-free access; toilet has no grab rails (CAMRA).
tips: Two minutes' walk from Buoy and Oyster and the Lifeboat – an easy Old Town micropub crawl.

name: Ales of the Unexpected, Westbrook (Margate)
summary: Long, narrow micropub on the Canterbury Road at Westbrook, on the 8/8A bus route from Birchington; quizzes and cribbage.
description: Ales of the Unexpected is a micropub on Canterbury Road in Westbrook, on the Birchington side of Margate and directly on the main bus route from Birchington. It is long and narrow, with a quiet seating area at the front and the bar and a livelier snug at the back. A handful of changing cask ales are served, along with real cider. It has a strong community feel, with regular quiz nights, cribbage on Monday evenings and frequent live music on Sunday afternoons. Families and dogs are welcome and there is a little outdoor seating at the front.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (updated June 2026): Mon-Sat 17:00-22:00, Sun 12:00-15:30.
accessibility: Step-free access; toilet has no grab rails (CAMRA).
tips: Stagecoach buses 8/8A from Birchington stop within 50 m; Margate station is about 400 m away.

name: The Laughing Barrel, Cliftonville
summary: Cliftonville micropub with 6-8 cask ales and a big cider and perry range, mostly from Kentish producers.
description: The Laughing Barrel opened at the end of April 2018 in part of the ground floor of a late-1960s estate pub on Summerfield Road in Cliftonville, with the rest of the building turned into a pharmacy. It is known for the range on offer: six to eight real ales and a large selection of ciders and perries, all served on gravity from a cooled room behind the L-shaped bar. The emphasis is on Kentish producers such as Wantsum and Goody, with beers from further afield as well. Opening is mainly evenings plus weekend afternoons, so plan around it.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (last updated Aug 2024): Wed-Thu 18:00-21:00, Fri 18:00-22:00, Sat 15:00-22:00, Sun 12:00-18:00; closed Mon-Tue. Check before visiting.
tips: Best for cider fans – one of the widest cider and perry choices in Thanet.

name: Hair of the Dog micropub, Minster-in-Thanet
summary: Village micropub in a former hairdresser's on Minster High Street; Good Beer Guide-listed, cash only.
description: Hair of the Dog took its name from the premises it occupies: a former hairdresser's shop on the High Street in Minster, the village south of Manston with its ancient abbey. Beers are served by gravity from a cooled room behind the bar and usually include Kentish ales such as Wantsum's, plus real cider. It was runner-up in Thanet CAMRA's Micropub of the Year in 2022 and appeared in the Good Beer Guide 2023. It makes a good stop after visiting Minster Abbey or walking the nearby marshes.
tips: Cash only. Minster has a railway station on the Ramsgate-Canterbury line.

name: The Conqueror Alehouse, Ramsgate
summary: Thanet's first micropub (opened 2010), now on Grange Road; nautical décor, gravity-served ales and ciders.
description: The Conqueror is credited as Thanet's first micropub, opening in 2010, and it has moved premises twice since while keeping its name. It was originally named after the paddle steamer Conqueror, though the sign now shows William the Conqueror. Today it occupies a small two-level shop on Grange Road on the west side of Ramsgate, with nautical touches, seating and the counter downstairs and ales and ciders served by gravity from chilled cabinets upstairs. There is always at least one local beer, plus cider and perry, bar snacks and occasional pop-up food nights. It is quiet and dog friendly and has a small garden.
opening_hours: Per Kent CAMRA: Sun-Thu 12:00-21:00, Fri-Sat 12:00-22:00.
tips: Combine with a visit to The Grange and St Augustine's (Pugin's buildings) nearby.

name: The Hovelling Boat Inn, Ramsgate
summary: Friendly micropub by Ramsgate harbour in a building that was a pub of the same name until 1909; pétanque at the back.
description: The Hovelling Boat Inn on York Street, a short walk up from Ramsgate's Royal Harbour, revives the name of a pub that traded in the same building until 1909; 'hovelling' was the local term for salvaging and servicing ships off the Goodwin Sands. It is now a welcoming micropub with up to six beers chalked up and served by gravity from a stillage at the back. There is no hot food, but generous filled rolls are usually available, with occasional pop-up food events. On warm days you can play pétanque in the area behind the pub.
opening_hours: Per Kent CAMRA: Mon-Thu 11:30-21:00, Fri-Sat 11:30-22:00, Sun 12:00-21:00.
tips: Two minutes from the harbour – good after a seal trip or the Ramsgate Tunnels.

name: The Pub, Ramsgate (micropub)
summary: Simple High Street micropub in Ramsgate with cellared cask, craft keg, occasional German draught and takeaway cans.
description: The Pub on Ramsgate High Street is a plain-speaking micropub that puts the emphasis on drinking and conversation. Inside it is dark wood and exposed golden brick, bright with daylight from the shopfront. The beer range covers cask ales from the cellar, craft keg, the odd German beer on draught and a fridge of cans, and you can buy beer to take away. It began as part of a small franchise and is now independently run. Being on the High Street it is a handy stop between the station and the Royal Harbour, and the Hovelling Boat and Montefiore Arms are both within a short walk.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (updated Oct 2026): Tue-Thu 16:00-22:00, Fri 12:00-22:00, Sat 12:00-23:00, Sun 12:00-21:00; closed Mon.

name: Mind the Gap micropub, Broadstairs
summary: Railway-themed two-level micropub by Broadstairs station, with gravity-served ales and ciders and live music.
description: Mind the Gap opened in July 2016 in a former shop on Broadstairs High Street, close to the railway station, which explains the name and the railway theme: there is even a length of mainline rail used as a foot rail upstairs. Seating and the counter are on the ground floor, with real ales and ciders served on gravity from chilled cabinets behind the bar. It is independent, dog friendly and hosts live music, and it marked its tenth anniversary in July 2026. Handy for anyone arriving in Broadstairs by train before heading down to Viking Bay.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA: Wed-Sat 14:00-22:30; Tuesday alternate weeks only (Kent CAMRA). Check Sun-Mon hours locally.
tips: Right by Broadstairs station – two stops from Birchington via Margate.

name: The Butcher's Arms, Herne – the first micropub
summary: The tiny former butcher's shop where Britain's micropub movement began in 2005; seats about a dozen, cash only.
description: The Butcher's Arms in Herne village, just inland from Herne Bay, is generally credited as Britain's first micropub. Martyn Hillier opened it in November 2005 in a former butcher's shop that he had been running as an off-licence, and its success inspired hundreds of similar one-room pubs, including the many now in Thanet. The original butcher's chopping blocks still serve as tables, there is seating for about twelve with standing room for a few more, and cask ales are served straight from the barrel with beer to take home too. It has won several CAMRA awards, including East Kent Pub of the Year in 2009. New managers took over in May 2026 and extended the hours.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (updated July 2026, new management from May 2026): Wed-Fri 18:00-21:00, Sat-Sun 12:00-15:00; closed Mon-Tue.
tips: Cash only and no cashpoints nearby. Public car park on School Lane. Combine with Goody Ales (Herne) or Reculver.

name: Brogdale Collections – National Fruit Collection, Faversham
summary: Home of the National Fruit Collection's thousands of apple and fruit varieties: orchard walks, cider shop, chocolate maker.
description: Brogdale Farm outside Faversham is home to the National Fruit Collection, one of the largest collections of fruit trees in the world, including a huge range of apple, pear, plum and cherry varieties. Visitors can wander the orchards on self-guided walks or join guided orchard tours at weekends through the fruit season, and the site runs pick-your-own weekends, juicing workshops and cider-making courses in autumn, plus an Apple Fair and a January wassail. The farm's courtyard 'market place' has the Tiddly Pomme shop selling ciders, juices and fruit, a café, the Mad Cat craft brewery and Kakawa Artisan Chocolate's workshop, where you can book hands-on chocolate-making sessions. On Sundays from March to October a miniature railway runs.
opening_hours: Orchard walks Tue-Sun 10:00-16:00; guided tours weekends 11:30 and 14:00 until 1 Nov 2026. Tiddly Pomme shop Tue-Sun 10:00-16:00, closed 2 Nov 2026-28 Feb 2027. Café Tue-Sun 10:00-15:00.
price: Self-guided orchard walk: adult £10, under-16s free (2026).
tips: Wassail listed for 16 Jan 2027 and the Apple Fair for 2 Oct 2027. Faversham station is about 25 minutes' walk.

name: Kakawa Artisan Chocolate, Whitstable
summary: Kent chocolate maker's Whitstable shop for hand-made bars and flavours; hands-on chocolate workshops at its Brogdale base.
description: Kakawa Artisan Chocolate is a small Kent chocolate maker known for inventive flavour combinations. Its shop on Oxford Street in Whitstable sells its bars, slabs and treats, while chocolate-making happens at its base at Brogdale Farm near Faversham, home of the National Fruit Collection. There it has run small-group workshops in which you learn how chocolate is made, taste milk, white and very dark chocolate, then design and make your own bars and a slab or bark; children are catered for too. Private sessions for one or two people have also been offered. Check the website for current workshop dates and prices before travelling.
opening_hours: Whitstable shop listed as open daily 10:00-16:00 (Produced in Kent listing; check before visiting).
price: Private workshop £95 single / £175 couple (2022 listing – may have changed).
tips: Workshops are at Brogdale (Faversham ME13 8XZ), not in the Whitstable shop; slots are non-refundable.

name: Macknade Food Hall & Food Village, Faversham
summary: Long-established Faversham food hall with Kent produce, a wine store, café, seasonal street-food village and tasting events.
description: Macknade on the edge of Faversham has been part of Kent's food scene for more than 175 years and is now a large independent food hall packed with Kentish and continental produce, a butcher's and deli counters, a café and a separate wine store with a good Kentish wine section. From spring to autumn its outdoor Food Village adds street-food traders and live music, with late openings on the first Friday of each month. Macknade also runs tastings and events, such as wine evenings and whisky-and-chocolate pairings. It shares Selling Road with Boutilliers brewery, so it pairs well with Brogdale and Shepherd Neame for a Faversham food-and-drink day.
opening_hours: Food Village 2026 season (from 3 Apr): Thu-Sun 10:00-16:00, first Friday of month 10:00-22:00. Food hall: listings give Mon-Sat 09:00-18:00 (to 20:00 Thu-Fri), Sun 10:00-16:00 – check before visiting.
tips: Check the events page for ticketed tastings.

name: Offvine wine tours (from Ramsgate/Margate)
summary: Ramsgate-founded small-group wine tours to independent Kent vineyards – 'you drink, we drive' – including a Margate departure.
description: Offvine was founded by Ramsgate local Rachel Proctor on the simple idea of 'you drink, we drive': small groups are collected and driven to independent vineyards in Kent and East Sussex, so nobody has to stay sober. Tours typically visit two producers, with a winemaker-led look around and tastings, and the range includes a classic introduction to English wine, a natural and low-intervention wine tour, an English sparkling wine tour and a dedicated Margate departure, plus private and hen-party options. Group tours run mainly from spring until the end of September. It is the easiest way to visit vineyards from Birchington without a car.
address: Pick-up points given at booking (Thanet/East Kent stations)
opening_hours: Scheduled group tours until end of September; private tours on request. Dates via online booking.
price: 2026 website: Offvine Tour £125, Offvine Margate £125, Natural Wine Tour £130, English Sparkling Wine Tour £140, private tours £400.
tips: Book online (FareHarbor) or email rachel@offvine.co.uk. Map pin is Ramsgate station; confirm the pick-up point when booking.
